plan.title: AD lesional vs control DE + Hallmark pathways
plan.analytical_narrative: Twelve skin samples (6 AD-lesional, 6 control), raw Salmon gene-level counts (12000 genes x 12 samples after metadata join; 13th column presumably gene ID), unpaired, single batch. One sample (sample_01) is ~4x below median library size — DESeq2's design knowledge base is explicit that this sample must be kept and inspected, not dropped by default. The flow: (1) sample-structure QC (blind VST, PCA, sample-distance heatmap, library-size bar chart) to see where sample_01 falls and decide with a stated reason whether to exclude it; (2) minimal count pre-filter (>=10 counts in >=6 samples, the smaller group size) plus DESeq2's internal median-of-ratios normalization; (3) DESeq2 Wald test with an explicit AD_lesional-vs-Control contrast and apeglm shrinkage of the fold change, reporting shrunken and unshrunken LFC side by side; (4) BH-adjusted independent filtering at alpha 0.05 to call significant genes, with p-value histogram inspected as a diagnostic; (5) fgsea preranked GSEA against MSigDB Hallmark (2026.1, human) on the full ranked gene list using the Wald statistic, followed by Reactome and WikiPathways as secondary collections, since AD skin transcriptomes are known to show small coordinated shifts (e.g. lipid metabolism, keratinization) that a hard significance cutoff can miss; (6) a consolidated report with fit diagnostics (MA plot, dispersion plot), the reproducibility record, and explicit caveats about the length-correction status of the counts and the low-depth sample. The counts are described only as 'gene-level counts from salmon as delivered' with no statement of whether tximport length-scaling occurred and no per-sample quantification files supplied, so the model is fit directly on the counts with no length offset, and this is flagged as a caveat per the design-knowledge rule on unestablished import state — a shift in isoform usage between conditions could show up as apparent differential expression.

flags.message: If one sample has a library size several times below the median of the study, do not delete it in silence. Keep it through the sample structure QC, look at it on the PCA and on the sample distance heatmap, report its library size and its detected genes beside the others, and remove it only with a stated reason. The count models down-weight a low-depth sample through its size factor, thus removal is a judgment, not a default.

A quantifier name alone does not establish that the length correction occurred. If the counts come from Salmon, kallisto, or RSEM as a gene-level table, with no per-sample quantification files and no average transcript length table, the import state is not established. Ask for the per-sample quantification files, quant.sf, abundance.h5, or genes.results, or for the average transcript length table per gene and sample. If neither arrives, fit the count model on the counts as delivered, with no length offset, and state in the plan and in the report that the length offset is lost and that a change in isoform use can show as differential expression. Do not run tximport on a gene table, because tximport imports transcript estimates, and do not invent a length input.

If fewer than about 50 genes pass the significance threshold, do not run an over-representation test on that list. A hypergeometric test of a short list finds no category, and a change of the threshold changes the list and the result. Run the ranked method on the full list of tested genes instead, because it finds a set of genes with a small but coordinated change that no single gene shows. State the size of the significant list in the report.
